newsitem.title: FRANCE: French rappers to avoid jail after reviling police.
newsitem.headline: French rappers to avoid jail after reviling police.

text.p: An appeals court on Monday scrapped three-month jail sentences against two French rap singers for lyrics reviling the police, giving them suspended terms and fines instead.

Singers Bruno Lopez, also known as Kool Shen, and Didier Morville, called Joey Star, were sentenced to suspended two-month prison terms and fined 25,000 francs ($4,300) each for insulting the police at a concert last year.
The original sentences in November -- three months in prison with another three months suspended -- triggered fierce debate in France over censorship versus respect for public officials.

Even the public prosecutor at the appeal last month had urged the court in the southern city of Aix-en-Provence to impose fines rather than jail on the singers, who belong to the group NTM -- which stands for "Nique Ta Mere" (Fuck Your Mother) in street slang.
Police unions, who had hailed the initial judgment as a check on foul-mouthed attacks on law enforcers, had urged that the sentences be left unchanged.
The court action had been launched by 26 policemen who were on crowd control duty at a concert at which the band played.
They testified that the group used the lyrics:

"I piss on the courts. The police are the fascists and the murderers. It's those motherfuckers in blue and the courts who bust our balls all year round...our enemies are the men in blue and we piss on them."
The police union alleged that the singers again used unacceptable language at a concert in a Paris soccer stadium on June 15 and urged new Interior Minister Jean-Pierre Chevenement to crack down.
